newsitem.title: CHINA: China leader calls for faster stocks, futures laws.
newsitem.headline: China leader calls for faster stocks, futures laws.

text.p: China must speed up the drafting of long-delayed laws governing trading in stocks and futures, a senior parliamentarian said on Monday.
"Drafting and discussion of all the laws on the legislative schedule must be accelerated," said Tian Jiyun, vice-chairman of the National People's Congress, or parliament.

"We must continue to give priority to economic legislation and promulgate laws concerning the market economy, such as the State Assets Law, Securities Law and Futures Trading Law," Tian said in a speech to the congress's annual session.

Beijing is eager to bring order to its youthful stock markets, which are prone to wild, speculation-fuelled surges and falls, but the legislation needed to create a clear regulatory framework has been long delayed.
The Securities Law, which parliament had considered since 1993, was still under revision, the China Securities on Monday quoted a senior lawmaker as saying.
A draft Futures Trading Law had been submitted to lawmakers in early 1996, the newspaper quoted Dong Fureng, vice chairman of parliament's financial and economic committee, as saying.
Development of China's futures markets has been largely stalled since treasury bond futures were banned after a huge trading scandal in Shanghai in 1995.
Some commodity futures were also scrapped after becoming the target of frenzied speculation.
Analysts say the main obstacle to passing the laws on securities is disagreement among central government departments over how responsibility for regulation should be apportioned.
